newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: MEP WARNS OF "COMMUNIST COMEBACK" IN EAST EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: MEP WARNS OF "COMMUNIST COMEBACK" IN EAST EUROPE.

text.p: A senior Dutch member of the European Parliament expressed concern in Prague on Thursday about a leftward drift in elections around post-communist Europe of recent years.

"We are concerned about a tendency that is going on in Europe, especially in central and Eastern Europe...that old communist groups, the so-called new socialists or social democrats, are coming back," said Wim van Velzen, who is president of the European Union of Christian Democrats.
Van Welzen was speaking after meeting Czech Christian Democrat leader Josef Lux the day before voting begins in a second round run-off for the newly-created Czech Senate.
Former communists have regained power in Poland, Hungary and Bulgaria in recent years. But more lately there have been signs that the pendulum is swinging back in some former communist countries.

Van Welzen provoked uproar in Romania last month by accusing President Iliescu, a former senior communist, of trying to rig presidential elections. In fact Iliescu lost the elections last weekend to anti-communist Emil Constantinescu.

Anti-communists have also regained power in Lithuania and won the Bulgarian presidential election. In the Czech Republic, the centre-right Civic Democratic Party (ODS) swept the first round of Senate polls last weekend, albeit on a low turnout.

The Czech Christian Democrats, although a junior partner to the ODS in the centre-right coalition, actually want Social Democrats to win seats in the Senate to avoid the chamber being dominated by the ODS of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.

But van Velzen said he was worried to hear about unconfirmed reports that the Social Democrats wanted to cooperate with the little reformed Communists -- a theory which Klaus has pushed hard in order to discredit the opposition.

"I was worried to hear that even in the Czech Republic the socialist party is talking about coalition with the Communists. I do hope that the Czech Republic, the population here, will consider very well the choice that is at stake," he said.
